'''Myoken-shu''' (妙見宗) is a Buddhist sect that became independent from the [[Tendai sect]] on December 10, 1946. It is a member of the [[All Japan Buddhist Federation]] (全日本仏教会).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Myoken-shu {{!}} All Japan Buddhist Federation |url=http://www.jbf.ne.jp/member?id=15472 |website=www.jbf.ne.jp |accessdate=2022-02-14}}</ref> The sect was founded by Shonin Noma Nissho,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Myoken-shu Headquarters Hon-Taki-ji｜Religious Organization Database |url=http://www.rirc.or.jp/xoops/modules/xxxxx05/detail.php?id=258 |website=www.rirc.or.jp |accessdate=2022-02-14 |publisher=International Institute for the Study of Religions}}</ref> with Shonin Noma Shusen as its patriarch. Its headquarters is located at [[Hon-Taki-ji]] Temple. The sect primarily consists of {{ill|Shugenja|en|Shugenja|qid=Q7504680|lt=Shugenja|1=Shugenja}} (ascetics) who practiced at the waterfall within the temple grounds. The principal deity is [[:en:Shakyamuni Tathāgata Buddha|Shakyamuni Tathāgata Buddha]],<ref name=":0" /> with secondary deities {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myōken|1=Myōken}} (Myoken Daibosatsu) and [[Jotomi Daibosatsu]].<ref name=":0" /> The sect's main scripture is the {{ill|en:Lotus Sutra|en|en:Lotus Sutra|qid=Q861212|lt=en:Lotus Sutra|1=Lotus Sutra}} (妙法蓮華経).<ref name=":0" /> At the headquarters Hon-Taki-ji, rituals combine the liturgical style of the [[:en:Nichiren sect|Nichiren sect]] with elements of [[Esoteric Tendai Buddhism]] (台密) and [[Shugendō|Shugendo]].

Shonin Noma Nissho received permission in June 1921 to relocate the temple named Kunko-in, which was renamed "Hon-Taki-ji" in November 1926.<ref name=":0" /> The main hall was completed in 1935.<ref name=":0" /> On December 10, 1945, the sect formally transitioned from the Tendai sect to establish the new sect "Myoken-shu," which continues to the present day.<ref name=":0" />

While the attire of Myoken-shu clergy resembles that of Nichiren priests, and practitioners chant the [[:en:Odaimoku|Odaimoku]] (sacred chant of Nichiren Buddhism), the sect exhibits significant differences. The Hon-Taki-ji headquarters lacks the [[Mandala of the Lotus Sutra]] (法華曼荼羅), there is no formal [[Nichiren doctrine]], no commemorative events for Saint {{ill|Nichiren|1=Nichiren|2=ja|3=日蓮|4=ko|5=니치렌|6=de|7=Nichiren|8=es|9=Nichiren|10=fr|11=Nichiren|12=it|13=Nichiren|14=nl|15=Nichiren|16=no|17=Nichiren|lt=Nichiren|qid=Q311478en|Nichiren|1=Nichiren|2=ja|3=日蓮|4=ko|5=니치렌|6=de|7=Nichiren|8=es|9=Nichiren|10=fr|11=Nichiren|12=it|13=Nichiren|14=nl|15=Nichiren|16=no|17=Nichiren|lt=Nichiren|qid=Q311478qid=Q311478|lt=Nichiren}}, and no rigorous ascetic training (荒行). Furthermore, the sect does not inherit the traditional Nichiren esoteric prayer rituals (法華祈祷) but instead conducts simplified rituals based on its own adaptations of Nichiren practices. Some affiliate temples have priests who have completed Nichiren-style ascetic training, but this is rare.
